svg.text: Two kinds of product (0013 §4)
weida — a new QUIC messaging protocol
the protocol, its Rust/Python library and the built core of the L2 broker
Guarantee dimensions — a tuple, never one enum
delivery · acknowledgement/completion · ordering · deduplication
backpressure · producer naming · control isolation (seven, closed list)
core is the floor, and a configured set may only be a superset of it
Transports — one variant each, below one boundary
QUIC (quinn) · inproc · AF_UNIX (Linux, macOS) · named pipes (Windows)
Req/Rep 1 KiB: 13 µs inproc, 51 µs unix, 58 µs QUIC (IMPLEMENTATION §4.13)
all four transports built; named pipes Windows-gated
Patterns — transport-blind above the boundary
Req/Rep · Push/Pull · Pub/Sub · PAIR · SURVEY · BUS
cursors orthogonal; all six in async Rust, blocking Rust and Python
broker: admission · credit · settle/requeue; store + cluster pending
Proof
tests/transports.rs runs all six patterns over QUIC, inproc, AF_UNIX
and named pipes unchanged; broker settlement is proved by behavior tests;
broker guarantee claims are asserted at the hop that earns them
the competitors, first-class in Rust
standalone: a library names its codec and weida-runtime, never weida
weida-zmq
11 socket types, 3 transports, 98 option rows, NULL/PLAIN/CURVE with ZAP
interop in both roles against libzmq 4.3.5 and zmq.rs 0.6
weida-nng
11 SP protocols, contexts, 48 option rows, TLS and IPC credentials
11 interop tests against NNG 1.4.0-rc.0 through the nng crate, both roles
weida-mqtt
MQTT 5 client: both QoS machines, subscriptions, retain, Will, aliases, AUTH
interop against rumqttd 0.20.0 and rmqtt 0.23.1; 6 disagreements measured
weida-amqp
AMQP 1.0 client: 9 performatives, both credit schemes, settle modes
interop in both roles against fe2o3-amqp 0.18.4
weida-nats
Core NATS client: 12 verbs, both wildcards, queue groups, inbox reply
interop written and not run — no nats-server; its clause 4 says "not met"
Python — five competitor bindings, one foundation
weida-zmq-py · weida-nng-py · weida-mqtt-py · weida-amqp-py · weida-nats-py
asyncio first, then sync; five wheel artifacts plus weida-py on the left
pending: MQTT's and AMQP's server halves, and a NATS interop run
Shared foundation — both products stand on it, and it knows neither protocol
weida-runtime — Exec, the three reactor owners, the capped resolver, AF_UNIX hygiene, the name registry · weida-core — addresses, limits, errors
weida-py-core — one exception class per errno variant, the asyncio bridge, the bytes boundary. No library depends on weida or weida-protocol (0013 §4.2)
Sources: docs/decisions/0013 §4 (two kinds of product), 0014 §2 (four workstreams, one PyO3 foundation), docs/libraries/*.md, docs/STATUS.md.
